#2072. GdS: Krösche announcement could come next week – how he will operate at Milan

Further confirmation has arrived that Markus Krösche will be joining AC Milan, and an announcement could come before the month ends.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm the news that been circulating for weeks now: an agreement has been reached with Krösche, and next week could be the perfect time to announce it to the world, at least as per the German director and the club’s plans.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

In short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

Krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

“Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche said upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”

The club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

#2071. Swansea City identify manager with 2.32 points per game as leading contender to replace Vitor Matos

Swansea City are pursuing a new head coach after Vitor Matos left his role at the Swansea.com Stadium to take charge of RC Strasbourg. Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kris O’Leary are leading the Swans on an interim basis, but ground is quickly being made in the search for a new boss.

According to a report from The Telegraph, the club have identified Icelandic manager Freyr Alexandersson as the leading candidate for their vacant head coach position. Talks have been held between the 44-year-old and the Championship club, and he appears to be their prime target at present.

Alexandersson is currently the manager of Norwegian side Rosenborg BK, who appointed him on a three-year contract in June. He has overseen 14 wins in his 19 games in charge of the club, recording a points-per-game rate of 2.32.

Alexandersson is a 44-year-old coach who has held a variety of roles in the dugout since beginning his coaching career back in 2008. He spent seven years at Leiknir Reykjavik as a player before moving into management.

The Swansea City target started out in women’s football, managing club team Valur before a short spell in charge of former club Leiknir Reykjavik. Alongside this role, Alexandersson spent five years as manager of the Iceland women’s national side.

He then stepped into the men’s setup as an assistant to Erik Hamren and Arnar Vidarsson before a short spell as a No. 2 at Al-Arabi. From 2021 though, Alexandersson has worked strictly as a first-team boss in men’s football.

He spent nearly three years in charge of Danish side Lyngby BK and 11 months at KV Kortrijk in Belgium before moving to SK Brann in Norway. Impressive work there saw him poached for the Rosenborg BK job, where he has continued to impress.

Swansea City head coach contender Alexandersson prioritises man management, working closely with his players to build strong relationships and placing importance on leadership. He has a strong reputation for developing players, which will appeal to the Swans too.

Tactically, his Rosenborg side set up in a 4-3-3 primarily, but he has used 5-3-2 or 3-5-2 formations in the past. Much like Matos, his teams press aggressively in the final third, and he demands frequent chance creation with players directed to suffocate opponents on and off the ball.

In terms of tactical similarities, Alexandersson feels like a great fit for Swansea City. The fact he wants his players to press high and play forwards much like Matos means that there can be a smooth transition into the new management.

Bringing in a boss with completely different ideas could bring teething problems. This squad has been built to play on the front foot with and without the ball, and Alexandersson will ensure they do so.

The Jamestown Analytics influence feels clear with this pursuit. They pride themselves on finding gems in lesser-used markets, and Alexandersson could be the latest top boss uncovered.

After initial talks, time will tell whether the Swans can strike a deal to bring Alexandersson to Wales.

#2070. L'aiuto di Candela, delusioni e gaffe. Totti a "Belve" parla di tutto: "Maurizio Costanzo mi disse..."

È un Francesco Totti che parla a cuore aperto, quello presente negli studi di Rai 2 ospite del programma "Belve" condotto da Francesca Fagnani. La conduttrice ha incalzato l'ex capitano della Roma - nello spirito e col timing tipico del format - portandolo tra una gaffe e l'altra su tantissimi temi non strettamente legati al mondo del pallone.

"Lei ha detto di non poter fare l'allenatore perché troppo buono...", una delle domande della Fagnani che trova subito conferma nella risposta di Totti: "Quando sei dall'altra parte è tutto più semplice. Mettendomi nella posizione dell'allenatore che deve scegliere per forza 11 giocatori, mi dispiacerebbe non farli giocare tutti…". Non manca spazio all'ironia che ha da sempre (o quasi) contraddistinto Totti: "Prima ero molto più rosicone. Poi Maurizio Costanzo mi fece cambiare idea, invitandomi al suo programma e dicendomi di essere più autoironico, di non prendermela per quello che dicevano. Da quel giorno mi è cambiata la prospettiva in meglio".

Dopo aver dato una spiegazione alla sua popolarità che va oltre quella di una normale persona famosa ("Forse è l'amore che ho dato a questa città, non l'ho mai tradita e mai gli ho girato le spalle"), Totti affronta anche il filone legato alla Roma: "Nel 2004 potevo andare a Madrid. La testa lo voleva ma il cuore no. Alla fine è stata la decisione più giusta. Al Real avrei vinto di più. Il Pallone d'Oro? Col Real avrei avuto più possibilità, con la Roma era più difficile".

Inevitabile tornare sull'addio alla Roma. Fagnani chiede: cosa cambierebbe del finale per renderlo meno doloroso? Totti risponde senza pensarci troppo: "Avrei cambiato il modo di comportarsi della società nei miei confronti. Avrei preferito che mi rispettassero di più dopo quello che ho fatto. Ho lottato fino a sei mesi prima che finisse, a dicembre ho mollato mentalmente per quello che stavo ricevendo da persone che non mi sarei mai aspettato".

E dopo l'addio al calcio? "Una mini depressione - continua Totti - , mi ero chiuso in me stesso. Poi gli amici e i familiari mi hanno aiutato. Tra i miei amici nel mondo del calcio mi hanno aiutato molto Candela e Vito Scala".

Qualcuno si è mai approfittato della sua posizione? "Diciamo persone impensabili, persone molto vicine a me, familiari, amici, parenti. Brutto dirlo ma hanno mangiato abbastanza un po' tutti, però non rinnego niente. Alla fine l'ho fatto col cuore e la generosità. Poi però passa il tempo, le strade si dividono capisci quello che è successo realmente in quei momenti".

Tornare alla Roma? "Non so più che dire. Quando sarà, se succederà, lo saprete. La porta on si chiude mai a nessuno, ma in questo momento io e la Roma abbiamo percorsi diversi, io sto bene e loro stanno facendo un grande lavoro. O si parte da zero o non si parte. Ma non è nessun messaggio".

#2068. More games, less issues: How Milan’s current injury situation compares to one year ago

In the past few weeks, Ruben Amorim has been battling a long list of absences due to injuries, but how does it compare to one year ago?

The second international break brings a useful moment to pause and reflect on the injury issues within the squad. Given that there have been at times as many as eight players out, it feels as though Amorim has been rowing against the tide a bit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese asks for a physically demanding style and he consistently emphasises the importance of proper rotation. Yet, at present, the likes of Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Strahinja Pavlovic are all out.

From Stefano Pioli’s final years into Massimiliano Allegri’s one-season stint, there was a recurring problem of muscle issues. For example, last season – despite no European football – the Rossoneri suffered 31 total injuries during the season, leading to a crisis at certain points.

In the previous season, which included the Champions League, the figure hit 33. In Pioli’s last season in 2023-24, he battled a staggering 40 different issues. How does the current season compare to the last though? MilanNews provide the data.

1. Pulisic – Ankle sprain – July 26 to August 12, 17 days out during the summer. 2. Leao – Right calf elongational injury – August 17 to September 25, 39 days out and missed 5 games. 3. Jashari – Compound fracture of the right fibula – August 28 to October 30, 63 days out. 9 games missed so far. 4. Pavlovic – Flexor problem – from September 14 to September 18, 4 days out. 5. Maignan – Right calf problem – from September 14 to September 23, 9 days out and 1 game missed. 6. Tomori – Right aductor strain – from September 28 to October 3, 5 days out. 7. Saelemaekers – Right flexor injury – from October 11 to October 18, 7 days out. 8. Estupinan – Ankle problem – from October 11 to October 30, 19 days out and 3 games missed. 9. Pulisic – Right thigh hamstring injury – from October 11 to November 5, 25 days out and 4 games missed. 10. Rabiot – Left soleus injury – from October 16 to November 18, 33 days out and 5 games missed. 11. Loftus-Cheek – Muscle strain – October 18 to October 27, 9 days out and 2 games missed. 12. Nkunku – Toe problem – October 16 to October 23, 7 days out and 1 game missed. 13. Leao – Hip problem – October 28 to October 30, 2 days out. 14. Tomori – Knee problem – October 28 to November 1, 4 days out. 15. Gimenez – Ankle problem and arthroscopic surgery – October 28, 2025 to March 21, 2026, 114 days out and 22 games missed.

Total: Seven traumatic/other and eight muscular in 13 matches played (11 Serie A, 2 Coppa Italia).

1. Pulisic – Bone edema at the junction of the tibia and fibula, July 8 to August 21. 44 days out during preseason. 2. Gila – Right rectus femoris strain, July 25 to August 12. 18 days out during preseason. 3. Gabbia – Ankle problems, September 1 to 11. 10 days out and missed 1 game. 4. Saelemaekers – Right ankle problem and subsequent surgery, since September 29. 5. Gabbia – Left thigh flexor injury, with partial tendon involvement, since October 11. 6. Chukwueze – Left hip tensor fascia latae tendon rupture, resulting in surgery, since October 21. 7. Ramos – Calf muscle overload, October 21 to 23. 2 days out and missed 1 game. 8. Gila – Overuse inflammation in the left ankle, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 9. Rabiot – Right calf strain, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 10. Moreira – Left calf flexor strain, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 11. Loftus-Cheek – Left medial flexor injury, from October 25. 12. Tomori – Right medial flexor injury, from October 29. 13. Pavlovic – Renal colic, from November 4 to 17. 13 days out and missed 2 games.

Total: Five traumatic/other and eight muscular from 15 matches played (11 Serie A, 4 Europa League).

So, while things might have felt quite bleak at various moments when gazing into a packed treatment room, Amorim has actually had a bit more luck than his predecessor when it comes to physical issues. Now he must hope that continues, or even that he gets luckier still.

#2067. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

#2066. EFL expert singles out ‘very good’ Wolves man for high praise ahead of Derby County clash

Wolves have handed the winger plenty of game time over the past 12 months or so, despite his tender age. He has become a key member of WWFC’s first-team squad over recent times.

Mane, 19, is under contract at Molineux until the summer of 2029. He has made 18 appearances for the Midlands outfit in all competitions this season, 16 of which have come in the Championship, and he has chipped in with three assists.

Maxwell has delivered his verdict on the youngster on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “Mane we hold to very high standards because we think he’s a very, very, very good player. It is always worth remembering he only turned 19 two months ago. He’s such a young player still.

“If you look at Championship minutes this season, he’s the second youngest player behind Ryan Kavuma-McQueen to have played more than 600 minutes. He’s in a little bucket there with Kavuma-McQueen, who’s still 17, then Mane and (Divine) Mukasa, who has just turned 19, and then Romelle Donovan, who is just about to turn 20.”

Wolves will be pleased that they managed to keep hold of Mane over the summer. WWFC were relegated from the Premier League earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with West Ham and Burnley.

Mane, who is an ex-England and Portugal youth international, was linked with an exit in the last transfer window. However, nothing materialised in the end and he stayed put beyond the deadline back in early September.

Many expected the teenager to take the second tier by storm but things haven’t exactly panned out like that. He still hasn’t scored and probably hasn’t made the impact in the EFL he would have hoped to before a ball was kicked this term.

Nevertheless, he is starting to find his feet now and is a promising talent. He will get better with experience and his game is still developing.

Mane looked good against Charlton Athletic for Wolves last time out. He caused problems for WWFC’s last opponents and helped them win 2-1 after goals by Adam Armstrong and Rafiki Said.

Cesar Peixoto’s side are back in action on Tuesday night as they aim to keep their momentum going. They face another match on their own patch against Derby County.

The Rams are in poor form and are in the drop zone along with Burnley and Preston North End. They have won only twice in the league and are five points from safety behind both Lincoln City and Watford after their 2-0 loss at Southampton over the weekend.

Wolves will fancy their chances of securing another win to boost their promotion push as they chase down the top two Middlesbrough and Stoke City. They are currently sat in 3rd place in the table after 16 fixtures and they are in the play-offs along with Birmingham City, West Brom, Southampton, QPR and Swansea City.

#2065. Como, Milla per 6 milioni è oro colato. E sarebbe potuto arrivare già lo scorso gennaio

Il Como ha un'altra pepita d'oro in casa, ma non è un giovanotto. Anzi, a 32 anni Luis Milla ha deciso una partita di Champions League tutto da solo contro il roccioso AEK Atene grazie a una conclusione a giro favolosa e dritta all'incrocio per superare Strakosha e regalare tre punti per raggiungere un clamoroso terzo posto in Europa. Intanto il playmaker spagnolo si sta rivelando sempre più imprescindibile nello scacchiere di Cesc Fabregas, mentre si gode la sua seconda giovinezza sul Lario. Il primo gol con la maglia biancoblù e pure quello in carriera in Europa dopo appena 5 partite.

E pensare che Milla è stato inseguito a lungo, quasi un anno, se non di più dalla dirigenza del Como. Infatti il ds Carlalberto Ludi, sospinto dalla voglia matta di Cesc Fabregas, voleva disporre di un altro volante di centrocampo già lo scorso gennaio almeno. In ritardo di almeno sei mesi, l'ex Getafe è sbarcato al Sinigaglia alla cifra irrisoria di 6 milioni di euro in estate: una carta rara del mazzo che i lariani non intendono scambiare o perdere. Per nessun motivo. Con una voglia smisurata di bruciare le tappe, superato a pieni voti il periodo di maturazione, tra Italia e Champions Luis sta raccogliendo i frutti di una carriera tortuosa e accidentata, con tanta gavetta in Spagna. Ostacoli lungo il percorso che gli hanno permesso di raggiungere un livello di esperienza e reazione al problema esemplare. La centralità nell'undici titolare oggi è palese, come l'impiego (1113 minuti in 17 gare complessive) e la continuità di rendimento, perché il 32enne non rifiata dall'11 ottobre contro la Roma (solo 2 minuti in campo). Chissà se la rete con l'AEK segnerà anche l'inizio di un ruolino di segnature stagionali.

Fabregas e il Como avrebbero voluto ingaggiare Milla già lo scorso mercato invernale quando invece hanno virato verso Adrian Lahdo al fotofinish: l'opportunità si era presentata proprio nell'ultimo giorno di mercato invernale, ma lo spagnolo non se la sentiva di lasciare il Getafe nel bel mezzo del campionato per via della situazione complicata che stava attraversando in termini di classifica. Meglio tardi che mai: a 32 anni ha preso le redini del centrocampo biancoblù e non intende più lasciarle. Il contratto firmato fino a giugno 2029 invece un attestato di stima importante non solo nei confronti del suo allenatore catalano ma anche del progetto del club lariano. Ad oggi una scelta che lo ripaga appieno.

#2063. Priorità ai terzini: ecco la shortlist con tutti i nomi per il Milan. Già a gennaio

Il mercato di gennaio si avvicina e in casa Milan c'è una priorità che prende sempre più corpo: rinforzare le corsie esterne. La fascia sinistra, in particolare, è uno dei reparti sotto osservazione, ma l'attenzione della dirigenza rossonera non si limita a quella zona del campo. L'obiettivo è individuare profili che possano alzare il livello delle alternative a disposizione di Ruben Amorim, con caratteristiche e costi differenti. Sono diversi i nomi finiti nell'orbita milanista, alcuni già conosciuti, altri emersi nelle ultime settimane.

Il profilo che stuzzica maggiormente è quello di Noussair Mazraoui. Il laterale marocchino del Manchester United è un giocatore che Ruben Amorim conosce bene e apprezza, avendolo già allenato in Inghilterra. La sua duttilità, la capacità di interpretare entrambe le fasce e l'esperienza internazionale lo rendono un'opportunità da tempo sul taccuino degli scout rossoneri, può darsi lo sia anche del nuovo HOF, Markus Krosche. I Red Devils devono fare riflessioni sui giocatori in rosa ora che è arrivato Mauricio Pochettino. Poi c'è Givairo Read, come anticipato su queste colonne: l'esterno basso del Feyenoord, classe 2006, è un profilo di prospettiva, dotato di qualità atletiche e tecniche che lo rendono uno dei talenti più interessanti nel suo ruolo. La valutazione del club olandese, nell'ordine dei 25-30 milioni di euro e l'asta può scattare, per questo il Milan drizza le anenne sin da ora. Attenzione anche a Malo Gusto, terzino del Chelsea, altro nome finito nel radar rossonero. Il francese rappresenta un'opzione che può combinare gioventù ed esperienza, anche se la sua situazione a Londra e i costi dell'eventuale operazione rendono il quadro da monitorare.

Tra le idee più calde per l'esterno basso mancini c'è Mahamadou Nagida, classe 2005 del Rennes, profilo accessibile per costi ma chiaramente da inserire step by step in una rosa così ambiziosa. Poi Juan Miranda del Bologna, che già conosce la Serie A, e attenzione pure a Maxim de Cuyper del Brighton, giocatore apprezzatissimo ma pure costoso, sui 50 milioni come richiesta. Altro nome: Alejandro Balde del Barcellona, sul quale (in prestito) ci sarebbe anche l'interessamento della Juventus.

#2062. GdS: Cisse becomes a pillar as Amorim as experiments with four-man attack

Alphadjo Cisse has definitely been the breakout player of the season so far and Ruben Amorim has no intention of dialling down his presence in attack.

Milan had a very clear plan when they headed into the current season: Goncalo Ramos would be the main man in attack. Instead, however, it’s the underdog Cisse who has been running the show, while the Portuguese striker has been at the bottom in terms of output.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning (see image below), that’s why there cannot be – and likely won’t be – a Milan without Cisse in attack. Ruben Amorim now wants to build the attack around him, as opposed to introducing him every now and then.

The most recent clash, the 2-1 win against Genoa, was a good example of this. Amorim went for a bold formation with Cisse, Ramos, Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot together. A team with a lot of quality and an attacking-minded style.

It was a shape that reminded us of 2009-10, when Milan were guided by another foreign coach: Leonardo. He chose a very attacking-minded side with four attackers and two midfielders, which is something that Amorim almost replicated.

Modric and Rabiot in front of the defence (Pirlo and Ambrosini then) and the fantasy project with Pulisic, Moreira, Cisse, and Ramos, comparable to the Ronaldinho, Pato, Seedorf, and Borriello of the old days.

Despite this, the goals were scored after two mistakes by Genoa (even if Milan’s pressing helped), so the goal is to repeat the experiment against Frosinone and to increase its effectiveness, the experiment should be repeated tomorrow.

In that sense, Cisse will be important as he’s the top scorer: three goals in Europa League and five in Serie A. He has scored with both feet and his head, demonstrating a combination of talent and an eye for goal: characteristics that are very important for a team like Milan.

The average also speaks for itself: eight goals spread across 658 minutes means he scores a goal every 82 minutes.  Best of all, his versatility means that he can play as an attacking midfielder, a left-winger, and even as a centre-forward.

At just 20 years and 17 days old, thanks to the fifth goal in his ninth Serie A appearance, Cisse became the second-youngest player to reach the milestone in the first ten games with Milan, at least since 1994-95. Only Pato did it younger, at 18 years and 181 days.

Furthermore, he’s one of only three players born after 2006 (top five leagues) to have scored eight or more goals in all competitions, along with Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner, who also scored eight.

As the pink newspaper concludes, Ramos has also produced eye-catching numbers, but in this case in a negative sense: 1,191 minutes on the pitch, three goals scored, meaning one goal scored every 398 minutes.

#2061. Millwall team news and predicted XI to face Stoke City with Alex Neil facing striker decision

Millwall have struggled to replicate the form of last term which saw them finish in 3rd place. They currently languish in 16th place following three consecutive Championship defeats.

Injuries have plagued the Lions’ early-season endeavours, and a run of two victories in 10 outings, coming against lowly Preston North End and Derby County, has left supporters debating whether Alex Neil is the right man to take them forward.

There is no shame in falling to Birmingham City and West Brom, despite poor performances against the two promotion contenders. However, the Lions’ loss to QPR escalated the cause for concern when they were played off the park, not helped by Zak Sturge’s early dismissal.

Stoke City meanwhile are 2nd in the table after four consecutive wins. They defeated Birmingham City on Saturday despite playing much of the second half with 10 men after Luca Bombino’s sending off.

Sturge will serve his one-game suspension against Stoke City after denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity by pulling down QPR forward Paul Smyth.

The absences of Millwall duo Ryan Leonard and Tristan Crama have been felt in the backline, with the latter struggling with ongoing ankle problems while Leonard has been sidelined with a knee injury. Both are expected to make a return at the start of December.

A similar return timeframe is in the pipeline for Filip Marschall, who suffered an ankle ligament injury in their draw to Lincoln City in October.

Mathis Servais was among a number of Millwall’s summer arrivals who generated considerable excitement upon arrival, signing from Belgian outfit KV Mechelen. He has played just nine minutes of Championship football due to a hamstring injury and remains out here.

Jensen; Sykes, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; De Norre, Metcalfe; Neghli, Arconte, Lisbie; Ivanovic

Jensen started his first game in goal for the first time in two months against QPR, and the injury to Marschall means he has hold of the number one shirt ahead of Max Crocombe.

Caleb Taylor and Jake Cooper have been Neil’s go-to centre-back pairing this term, starting in all 16 Championship matches, and will likely continue their partnership with Mark Sykes set to start at right-back. The red card to Sturge means the left-back role is up for grabs, one which Alfie Doughty could fill against his former side with Jordi Osei-Tutu also another option.

Casper de Norre was withdrawn at half-time against QPR but should be fit to start alongside Jenson Metcalfe.

Promising wideman Kyrell Lisbie has been deployed on both flanks of the attack this term and will likely start on the left, with Camiel Neghli occupying the right as he looks to rediscover the form he showed last season.

Yet to score since drawing with Middlesbrough in September, Tairyk Arconte will look to rediscover his finishing touch as the Guadeloupe international looks set to line up in an advanced midfield role.

The responsibility of leading the line has fallen to Lyndon Dykes this term, but he has been part of a misfiring Millwall attack. As such, Serbian striker Mihailo Ivanovic could come in his place for only his second league start of the season.

Stoke City vs Millwall kicks off at 20:00 at the Bet365 Stadium and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Football.
