#1972. Chelsea co-sporting director Laurence Stewart to leave in leadership reshuffle

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

The departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

Arsenal are said to be trying to reward Piero Hincapié with better contract terms after just months since making his move permanent.

#1968. Arsenal mourns Peter Storey: 1971 Double-winning hero dies aged 81

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal have expressed their condolences in the passing of former player Peter Storey.

Storey was an influential member of one of the most successful sides in the club’s history. The midfielder appeared in 501 games for the Gunners between 1965 and 1977, winning the First Division and FA Cup during the 1970/71 season.

Storey was a key figure in the famous run as he helped keep the FA Cup hopes alive with a display against Stoke City.

A statement from the club confirmed his death on Tuesday (17th November). The club will pay tribute to Storey in their Champions League tie against Borussia Dortmund on 24th November.

Storey signed as an apprentice with Arsenal in 1961, and made his first-team debut in October 1965 in a game against Leicester City.

He was later converted to a central midfielder by manager Bertie Mee and coach Don Howe. Storey became an invaluable member of the squad due to his aggressive play, work-rate and versatility.

In 1970 Storey was part of the side that won the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, and the following year Arsenal won the league and FA Cup double.

Storey played a key role in an amazing FA Cup semi-final in April 1971. After Arsenal had looked like they were losing, Storey scored a last-minute penalty to make it 2-2.

Arsenal won the replay to get to the final, beating Liverpool to win their first-ever double.

Storey scored 17 goals in 501 games for Arsenal. This puts him in joint 8th place in the most appearances for the club.

Storey enjoyed success at club level and earned his first cap for England in 1971. He earned a total of 19 caps for England.

He played for England until 1973. In 1977, Storey left Arsenal to join Fulham, meaning he had a 12-year stint at the north London club.

He played 19 games for Fulham before retiring from professional football in 1978.

Following his football career, Storey had a difficult time. He was imprisoned for a number of crimes. In 2010, he wrote an autobiography, True Storey: My Life and Crimes as a Football Hatchet Man, detailing these events in his life.

He will be remembered in Arsenal history for his impressive contribution to the club. Having made 501 appearances for the club, he was a key member of the squad that won the Double in 1971.

Playing against Borussia Dortmund will be a great way for fans to pay tribute to one of the key players in a special time in the history of the club.

Arsenal head to St James’ Park this Saturday for their first match after the international break. They could be faced with a weakened Newcastle midfield.

#1966. Christos Tzolis challenges Arsenal critics with a message about his physicality

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Winger Christos Tzolis wants to prove he has a lot to offer Arsenal beyond his attacking prowess.

Since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium. The Greek attacker scored 17 goals and made 23 assists in 36 league games.

But doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League. In his first stint in England with Norwich City, he showed little sign of becoming the player he is now.

Since making his debut for the club, Tzolis has become a more rounded attacking threat. He has started all 7 Premier League games this season and provides a reliable option on the left for Arteta.

However, in recent comments, it seems that he is aware of the perceptions around his physicality and is keen to change them.

Tzolis spoke to Arsenal Media, saying that he doesn’t think the notion of him lacking the physicality to play at top level has validity.

He claimed that he is not a player without muscle and cited his accomplishments. He also described his tendency to use aggression against his opponents.

This is a key part of Arteta’s system at the club. Tzolis is expected to press from the flanks if Arsenal lose the ball.

Tzolis is comfortable with this role. He is able to track back well to support his full-back, adding an extra dimension to the left side.

The Greek international has proven his physical ability outside of match play. He was nicknamed Leonidas by the fitness team at the club due to a strong performance in pre-season.

It is reported that he completed the running challenge better than anyone in the squad.

Tzolis has joined Arsenal to add attacking flair to the squad, having left for Besiktas. He looks like he could be a formidable goalscorer and creator.

In the league last season, Tzolis contributed 40 goals and put in a good performance in Europe. This led to Arsenal spending a reported £34 million to bring him to the club.

He has not had the best impact in the league, registering just one assist and no goals, but this should not be taken to mean he is not contributing.

Tzolis has shown an ability to fit into Arteta’s style of play. His defensive contribution, work rate and combative nature may prove very valuable in tough away games.

Despite there being plenty to improve on, Tzolis provides more than just an attacking option for Arsenal.

If Tzolis can change people’s view of him in terms of his physicality and continues to put his technical skills and determination together, then he can be a valuable asset in Arteta’s plans.

Bournemouth’s determination to keep Alex Scott has done little to discourage Chelsea, who remain among the leading contenders to sign the England midfielder.

Chelsea are not alone in their admiration. Arsenal and Liverpool have also been linked with Scott, whose performances have attracted attention beyond the Premier League.

Suggestions circulating on social media that Bournemouth have already agreed to let him leave in January remain unsubstantiated. There has been no reliable confirmation of such an arrangement, and the club’s reported position is firmly against a winter sale.

#1962. Arsenal transfer dilemma: Alex Scott and Nico Paz could force difficult decisions for Arteta

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Potential signings of Alex Scott and Nico Paz may pose a challenge for Arteta.

While both players would add quality to the squad, their arrival would be a consideration for current players in the Emirates squad.

Scott would add quality in midfield, and Paz adds creativity and versatility going forward. Arteta must consider that adding these players may hinder the development of current players.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on bringing Alex Scott to the club.

After rejecting contract offers from Bournemouth, Scott could only have one year left on his contract at the club next summer. However, he is understood to be valued by Bournemouth at over £100m.

He would be a great addition for Arteta, with the versatility and skill he has. He could give added competition in midfield.

Yet his potential arrival raises questions about Myles Lewis-Skelly’s future role.

Myles Lewis-Skelly was included in the Champions League final line-up last season. He showed that he is trusted by the club.He has also demonstrated his commitment by remaining at the club despite opportunities to gain regular playing time at other clubs.

Signing another expensive midfielder may present difficulties. It is unclear at this point whether Scott will be a useful addition to the squad or simply overcrowd this area of the team.

Nico Paz presents another interesting option for Arsenal.

Paz joined Como from Real Madrid in the summer. He has caught the eye of a number of big clubs and has increased his appeal with strong performances in international football. The 22-year-old has scored 5 times in his last 5 games for Argentina.

Paz is a versatile right-sided player and could be an appealing addition to Arteta’s strike force.

There are already plenty of players fighting for attacking positions at Arsenal.

Bukayo Saka is key in the team’s attack, and with Martin Ødegaard and Noni Madueke in the squad too, there are plenty of options. Max Dowman is a young player looking to break into the first team.

While Paz would add quality to the squad, Arsenal would need to find a specific role for him. There are complications with the move, though. Real Madrid have an option to re-sign him in 2027 for 80 million euros.

Although Arsenal are facing challenges in attracting quality players to the club. They now also face issues in managing a squad with experienced internationals and developing young players.

Although Scott and Paz would improve the depth of the squad, players must not be sacrificed for new players if they have already shown quality.

Players such as Lewis-Skelly and Dowman may be negatively affected by this. Opportunities may be taken away from them if the club continues to spend large amounts of money on new players.

However, it is still very important for Arsenal to bring in quality players to compete for major titles.

Know how the additions will integrate within the playing style and how they affect the other players within the squad.

The Gunners can strengthen further without overloading the squad. Good additions can be made to the first XI whilst also providing a realistic chance for young players to come through from within the academy.

#1961. Chelsea make early move for Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. He also writes about Manchester City for Read Man City and motorsport for Read Motorsport. A former accountant, he became a freelance writer in 2011 and has written for BBC Sport and Metro.

Chelsea have reportedly made contact with Palmeiras as they attempt to gain an early advantage in the race to sign Brazilian teenager Eduardo Conceicao.

The 16-year-old forward has attracted attention from several leading European clubs, but Chelsea are understood to be among the first to establish direct contact with Palmeiras over a potential future transfer.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, the London club have held a series of discussions as they seek to position themselves ahead of their rivals.

Palmeiras are reportedly preparing for substantial offers, with some figures at the Brazilian club discussing a valuation as high as €100m (£85m).

That figure has not been established as a firm asking price, however, and Brus reports that industry sources expect the eventual cost to be lower. Chelsea’s previous investment of approximately £51m in Estevao is regarded as a possible benchmark.

Manchester City’s ownership group have also made contact regarding Conceicao, while Arsenal, Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs reported to have watched him.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with Palmeiras could help their efforts, although the level of competition means there is no guarantee that their early interest will lead to a deal.

The player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

No formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

#1959. Chelsea news: Stewart departure, Scott interest and Bournemouth preparations

Gary Gowers is a sports journalist and the editor of Read Everton, where he leads daily coverage of Everton news, transfers and analysis. Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

His departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

The changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

Scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s plans as well as any future discussions about his next move.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

After Saturday’s fixture, Chelsea travel to Hill Dickinson Stadium to face Everton on 17 October. Alonso will be looking for greater consistency as the domestic programme resumes.

#1958. Max Dowman’s Arsenal return: Is the teenage star one to watch, and can he keep his nose clean?

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Max Dowman shortly returns to action for Arsenal after serving a three-game suspension.

His absence has been disappointing, but the experience should give the youngster an important lesson. Can he put the incident behind him and show Mikel Arteta that he can be trusted?

Dowman received a red card against Fleetwood Town after kicking out at Harrison Neal. Arsenal appealed the decision, but the FA rejected the club’s appeal.

The suspension ruled him out of three domestic fixtures against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle United.

He’ll be back on 29 November as Arsenal take on Manchester City. This should give the young star a chance to get his season back on track and showcase what makes him such a highly-rated player.

Dowman looks very promising for the future. He has shown great adaptability playing with the more experienced players and has the self-belief to make an impact in games.

He has performed well in the Carabao Cup. In the 4-2 win against Ipswich, Dowman scored two goals, showing his flair and poise in front of goal.

Arteta has given him opportunities to play in the Premier League and Champions League, meaning that he appears to have a clear route into the first team.

Although Dowman still has a lot to learn, he displays great potential in his technical ability and combative nature. As he gets more games under his belt, fans will be excited to see how he progresses.

Dowman was sent off in an unfortunate moment. He was heavily challenged by Neal and, after lashing out, was shown a straight red card.

Although this one moment should not be enough to dismiss a young player from the game completely, it can serve as a valuable lesson on the pressure that comes with playing at a higher level.

Opponents will test Dowman physically, but he must learn to keep his composure. As he starts making an impact, some players may target his age and inexperience to unsettle him.

As he gets more game time, consistency will be key. Arteta must be confident that Dowman can be relied on in high pressure situations.

Arsenal do not need to rush Dowman into the first team. The squad’s quality allows Arteta to manage his minutes and give him time to develop without putting too much pressure on him.

If Dowman is to play against Manchester City, it will depend on Arteta’s plans, but he has certainly done enough to warrant consideration.

The suspension should not define his season. What matters now is how he responds, both on and off the pitch.

Dowman has the talent to become an important player for Arsenal. Keeping his discipline will be just as important as displaying his ability.

#1957. Arsenal transfer news: Why Kevin Schade could be a smart January signing

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal are looking to strengthen their attacking options in January. One player they are reportedly keeping an eye on is Brentford winger Kevin Schade. Mikel Arteta will be keen to add competition in attack, and Schade may be a good option.

Schade will give additional pace to the offence. He is capable of playing in multiple attacking positions to provide Arteta with extra depth in the squad.

However, it may be difficult to get Schade. He is on loan at Brentford, and may want to keep him in the long term. If Schade is seen as a key player in the future, they may be difficult to negotiate with.

Schade’s versatility is another big plus. His speed and straightforward method make him hard to deal with for defenders. In addition, he can be used as a left-sided attacker, giving Arteta more flexibility in his front line. As the club are playing in a number of competitions, this can be very useful.

Schade has already scored 3 times in the Premier League this season. He has quickly adapted to playing in England after moving from Freiburg to Brentford in 2023.

Despite only being 24 years old, Schade still has a lot to improve on. He has lots of experience in the Premier League but has not quite reached the peak of his ability yet. If he moves to Arsenal, he may be able to elevate his performance.

Brentford has already started negotiations with Schade regarding a contract extension that would keep him tied to the club for a long time. He is already contracted until the summer of 2028.

Arsenal’s interest could prove problematic. Other clubs are also keeping their eyes on this player. Tottenham in particular are not seen as a major threat at this stage.

It is going to be very challenging for Brentford to let go of Schade because he has played a key part in their offensive setup, and losing Schade could prove disastrous.

Arsenal will have to pay Brentford whatever they ask for, Schade, and since he has a decent amount of time left on his contract, Brentford has an edge in negotiations.

Arsenal’s interest in Schade is logical. His versatility will provide Arteta with additional flexibility because of his prior experience in the Premier League.

It can be considered positive to sign new strikers. Arsenal must decide if they believe that Schade will fit in well with their current players and whether the asking price from Brentford is reasonable.

As of now, there are no signs of a transfer on the horizon, but it is clear that Schade is a player worth monitoring as the winter transfer window approaches.

#1956. Young Hammer is ‘big money flop’ according to report – but West Ham fans won’t agree

In these days of instant access to everything, fame is sudden and success is apparently supposed to happen overnight. Criticism of West Ham’s team and their mid-table mediocrity is often swift and harsh. Even players who arrived in the summer are already being written off, according to supporters and news sites.

Which seems especially harsh considering the age and trajectory of several key players in this West Ham side.

How many ‘West Ham legends’ of the past would have been discarded after their first dozen games, I wonder, if they’d not been an immediate sensation.

Bad enough that so-called ‘fans’ took to booing Scott Parker’s very first home game at 90 minutes: Now it seems one of the youngest talents from the summer intake is already being labelled as a  ‘flop’.

That’s the flavour of a report out this evening from givemesport.com who claim that:

As they take aim at ..Edwin Austbø who, at just twenty one, has hardly had a chance to get settled in east London before he’s being labelled a’ big money’ (eh?) flop, despite his transfer fee being a modest £11 million. Perspective being everything, that’s about a quarter of a Kilman who cost £40 million and would surely be most people’s choice for the ‘big money flop’ label.

A flop? After three months? With two goals and two assists at just 21 years of age, I’d say Austbo is well on track to grow into the team.

“Expectations were also high that summer signing Austbo could prove to be an exciting addition in the second tier this term….He has two goals and two assists for the Irons so far this term, but you would probably expect his goal contribution numbers to be higher in a team which has scored 38 league goals…..

As things stand, Austbo is quickly becoming a big-money transfer flop, and he needs to improve quickly to start repaying his fee.”

Steady on, guys, This young man has huge talent, was not outrageously expensive and has already produced more goals and assists than players who cost twice his transfer fee. At least wait until the end of the season – his first in the English leagues – before writing him off.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Been thinking the same, about former greats not being given a chance today, due to constant demands for success and questionable expectations. Expectations, hopes, ambitions, all normal, but with any sport, you also need to be a bit of a fatalist I think and not expect it to happen tomorrow.

Look at Frank Lampard Snr, LB for 18 seasons and coming from the youth system, capped twice for England. 100% a club great who won trophies with WHU. Happened, because he was given plenty of chances to develop as a youth because he’ll have had bad games, maybe an occasional below-par season (normal unless you are Declan Rice) before everything clicked.

Current WHU team youngsters need their to chance to develop in the same way, because we have plenty of youngsters in and around the 1st team who have the potential to develop and become successful players. With the likes of Herrick, Golambeckis, Engels, Magassa, Mayers, Cummings, Fearon…. (there are too many!!) WHU team has a lot of potential – just add some savvy recruitment along the way.

For this to happen need a longer term sense of ambition (something DK & Koppen might well have) as opposed to short-term, but brief want for success. Too early for this team as it is a young team needing to develop before becoming reliable. Might be worth the wait though, because there is a lot of talent there and a burgeoning recruitment team.

Written without considering what they were saying. Austbo is yet to prove himself at West Ham, but hasn’t performed too badly, considering that he has not had a regular or consistent run in the team. Give him a chance.

We’ve more to worry about than a player with 4 goal contributions in the minutes played equivalent of 4.5 games!! .. If he keeps that ratio up, I’d be more worried about keeping hold of him than calling him an expensive flop!!! .. His direct competition for a place is Solomon who has 4 goal contributions in the minutes played equivalent of 11 games! .. I know the name I’d have on my team sheet and he’d be playing the whole game .. Whilst looking at these ratios, Kante has 5 goal contributions in the minutes played equivalent of 8 games, which might improve if he’s given license to run forward into space and where he can’t lose the ball in dangerous positions .. Stats aren’t everything, but having Austbo and Kante on the bench for pretty much half the time doesn’t make sense when we need goals to make up for the defending ..

when they, you say had big expectations, I didn’t speak to anyone or read anywhere that anyone in this country had ever heard of him ( outside of probably scouts). So not sure where the big expectations come from.

Think the phrase ‘flop’ should be reserved for those more richly deserving!!

Yeah, we now have a “West Ham” manager, with Mr. West Ham alongside him in the dugout. In the boardroom proper structures of a modern football club are being put in place. After so many years of poor management from the top to the team. It will take time, look at Man United, supposedly the worlds biggest club. #1955. Newcastle vs Arsenal: Team news, predicted line-ups and match preview

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal will have a tough task on hand as they visit St James’ Park.

Mikel Arteta’s side are five points clear at the top of the Premier League after their 1-0 victory over Hull City ahead of the international break. The Gunners have now gone nine games unbeaten in all competitions.

Despite only one win in their last six games, Newcastle will be a dangerous side at home.

Although Arsenal have won the last three encounters with Newcastle, recent games at Tyneside have not gone entirely smoothly for Mikel Arteta. He will also have to make a few key decisions in the squad with players injured and a busy run of fixtures.

Bruno Guimaraes will certainly be a topic of discussion for this game. The midfielder joined Newcastle four-and-a-half years ago, playing an important role in the development of the side, before moving to Arsenal on a reported 75 million pound move in the summer.

Whilst he has struggled to make himself an automatic starter in Arteta’s side, he could have a bigger impact with the absence of Martin Zubimendi.

Zubimendi is likely to be out for several weeks. Declan Rice should start, and Guimaraes is also likely to be involved, to form a double pivot.

Newcastle will try to play a gritty game to unsettle Arsenal. Despite Guimaraes’ knowledge of the opposition, he will have to assist the visitors to maintain control of the midfield battle.

Saliba is now back in contention after recovering from a back injury. The Frenchman has not played in the first team this season, but has made two appearances as he recovers. He played 45 minutes for the U21s.

Arteta confirmed that Saliba is in good shape and will begin to play more games, though he is unlikely to be in the starting line-up for the game against Newcastle.

Konsa should be in the starting line-up alongside Gabriel. Saliba could come on from the bench, as he looks to make his first competitive appearance of the season after the Champions League final last time out.

Saka is still unavailable due to quad trouble, whilst Dowman is suspended. Madueke should start on the right and Havertz will spearhead the attack.

Newcastle United: Predicted line-up not confirmed in the supplied team news.

Arsenal: Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Rice, Guimaraes; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz.

Arsenal absentees: Martin Zubimendi, Bukayo Saka and Max Dowman.

Saliba is available but is not expected to start.

Newcastle have leaked goals at home this season. However, with Madueke and Tzolis providing pace in wide areas, this should not worry Arsenal too much.

Nevertheless, this game should be challenging for the Gunners. Newcastle are dangerous in attack and can capitalise on errors quickly in possession.

Despite Arsenal’s solid defensive record, they have failed to keep a clean sheet in their 4 visits to St James’ Park.

Overall this should be a good watch with goals scored by both sides. However, Arsenal should be able to pick up some vital 3 points.

Predicted score: Newcastle United 2-3 Arsenal.

#1953. Kepa handed Arsenal opportunity to prove he can fill Raya’s boots against Dortmund

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

With David Raya out, Kepa Arrizabalaga has a great chance to prove that he is more than just an Arsenal cup keeper. Mikel Arteta needs to have confidence in his number two. He needs to ensure that he upholds the same high bar set by the starting keeper as Borussia Dortmund come to the Emirates.

Raya has been ruled out of tonight’s Champions League game following a shoulder problem which he picked up in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle United.

Whilst the initial diagnosis is good news, surgery is not required. Further tests will determine Raya’s recovery period.

As previously mentioned, Kepa will be stepping in for Raya at St James’ Park. Moreover, Arteta has stated his preferred choice of player in this situation. It seems that Illan Meslier will miss out on the opportunity to play this time.

As well as playing for Arsenal, the Spaniard has formerly played in the Champions League for Chelsea and Real Madrid. He has already appeared 14 times for the Gunners. Including in the league stage match which saw them beat Kairat Almaty.

Whilst Kepa has typically been second choice to Raya, his game time has mostly been in the EFL Cup. He will now need to prove himself as a trustworthy option for Arsenal should Raya be injured or otherwise unable to play.

As well as being a good goalkeeper, Raya is also good at passing and positioning. This in turn assists Arsenal in attacking from the back line.

Ex-Arsenal midfielder Paul Merson has acknowledged the quality that Spanish goalkeepers have at creating good defensive and central positioning. This can frequently be an under-recognised yet important component in Arsenal’s build-up play.

Like Arsenal, Kepa will also have to remain calm when playing out from the back. Although Kepa does not necessarily need to replicate all of Raya’s qualities, he will need to have good decision-making skills as well as good communication.

Meslier is still in contention, having played in the Carabao Cup game against Fleetwood Town. Kepa has been Arsenal’s number two keeper in the Premier League and was able to rush on in for Raya when he was substituted at Newcastle.

It does seem that Kepa is the obvious option, and he can further cement his position in Arteta’s team.

Arsenal’s schedule is demanding. They are playing Manchester City on a Sunday and there are also worries about Raya’s fitness. So far, the club has not yet received medical information on Raya’s status.

Then there is Dortmund. They have already secured victories in their first four games in the Champions League and are level on points with Arsenal in the league section.

Kepa does not have a great deal of flexibility. Arsenal require the new goalkeeper to offer them security.

In case Raya needs more time to recover, it is necessary for Arteta to be able to guarantee that there is an effective replacement.

For Kepa, it is equally an opportunity to prove that he can assume this leadership position for the team during important moments.

#1952. Portsmouth v West Ham Preview: Predicted XI As Parker Searches For First Win

Portsmouth v West Ham United EFL Championship, Fratton Park, Tuesday 24 November 2026, 7.45pm GMT

This is a crucial match for West Ham and Scott Parker, who has probably endured the shortest honeymoon period of any Hammers manager in recent memory. His first three games have produced a rousing comeback against Cardiff City, a forgettable defeat at Blackburn Rovers and Saturday’s frustrating 1-1 draw with Preston North End.

West Ham dominated possession and registered 30 attempts against Preston, yet never really looked clinical enough to score the winner. Indeed, had the referee awarded another 20 minutes of injury time, I’m still not convinced we would have found a second goal.

Parker is still waiting for his first victory as West Ham head coach, and Tuesday’s trip to Fratton Park represents another difficult assignment. Portsmouth have lost just once in eight Championship matches and sit only one point and two places behind the tenth-placed Hammers.

Ordinarily, one might expect Parker to do some tinkering after failing to beat the team at the bottom of the division. However, I suspect he won’t make sweeping changes because he was very pleased with the way his team performed against Preston.

Edson Alvarez – likely to become key in Parker’s plans this season

Parker said he got almost everything he wanted from the performance apart from the result, while describing Finlay Herrick and Edson Álvarez as “brilliant” in his post-match assessment. I’m not quite sure I would agree with that overall verdict, although the return of Álvarez was unquestionably a bonus.

The Mexican looked decent on his return to the team and provided some much-needed protection in front of the back four. Parker has probably made it clear that, for the remainder of this season, West Ham will play with a recognised holding midfielder.

Without wishing to sound like a scratched record, I still believe Jarrod Bowen needs to be used more centrally. Parker appeared to have been given the keys to unlocking West Ham’s attacking potential against Cardiff, but unfortunately he seems to have kept them in his back pocket ever since.

Bowen remains our most dangerous attacking player, yet watching him pinned to the right flank against Preston was depressing. West Ham lacked magic, invention and somebody willing to take responsibility in the areas where matches are won.

Mohamadou Kanté can consider himself unlucky not to have featured at all against Preston because he has been one of West Ham’s better players this season. There is an argument for playing him in the attacking midfield position at Portsmouth, where his pace and direct running could give Parker’s team something different.

However, I don’t think Parker will throw the baby out with the bathwater. He has already spoken about remaining stable and consistent, so I expect Divine Mukasa to retain his place behind Joël Piroe.

Piroe should continue up front, as much because of the lack of convincing alternatives as anything else. Manor Solomon could return on the left, with Parker perhaps deciding that his experience is better suited to a difficult night at Fratton Park.

I suspect there will be a change at left-back, with Ollie Scarles coming into the team. Max Kilman is available again after completing his one-match suspension and should immediately return alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos.

According to the club’s official team news, Alphonse Areola and Kyle Walker-Peters continue to be assessed. Unless Walker-Peters is unexpectedly declared fit, Joël Veltman should remain at right-back.

Portsmouth possess a worse attack than West Ham but a better defence, so this is unlikely to be an open game. They are only two places and one point behind us, while their recent results suggest Parker’s team will have to work extremely hard for anything at Fratton Park.

West Ham’s failure to convert possession into goals remains the obvious concern. However, if Parker can keep things tight defensively and finally find a way to make one of our attacking opportunities count, I believe the Hammers can edge it.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

No to Kilman, it’s been proven so many times we are better without him. I don’t understand why we keep going back to him, maybe its his price tag. I do however agree with using Bowen differently.

The only thing I’m asking is that we rewrite the script for once, do not go behind, then spend the rest of the match chasing the game. There’s only so many times that script can play out isn’t there ? It’s been like Groundhog Day.

Herrick was OK give him another shot, Alvarez a lot better than OK essential starter, Mayers not Scarles please, and give Piroe a run of games as he looks the best of not particularly inspiring options.

#1951. AC Milan Women 3-2 Sassuolo: Grimshaw crucial after crazy first half

Christy Grimshaw was crucial as AC Milan Women finally got back to winning ways, following what was a rather crazy first half against Sassuolo.

After two defeats and a draw, dropping points in a silly fashion against Napoli last weekend, Milan Women needed to bounce back with a win today. Thankfully, that’s exactly what they managed to do, even if it wasn’t the most controlled performance.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Just looking at the scoreline and the timing of the goals is enough to understand the nature of the game. All five goals were scored in the first half and it doesn’t end there either. All five were scored within the first 27 minutes!

The veteran Grimshaw opened the scoring for the Rossonere after nine minutes, but Sassuolo found a way back into the game just two minutes later. The Scottish international decided to restore the lead just four minutes later, i.e. in the 15th minute.

Angelica Soffia then made things more comfortable with a third goal in the 24th minute, or at least so we thought. Just three minutes after that, Sassuolo scored again and thus brought some life into the game, even if Milan looked the better side.

Suzanne Bakker’s side actually dominated possession, had more shots on target and also had a higher xG, so the win definitely feels deserved. And boy was it needed! The situation in the standings is still not great, but at least they are now four points behind the Champions League zone.

#1950. Barcelona: Why Flick rejected Bastoni, Laporte and Romero last summer

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:23

In their quest to strengthen their central defence last summer, Barcelona submitted the names of Alessandro Bastoni, Aymeric Laporte and Cristian Romero to Hansi Flick. None won the favour of the German boss.

It is no secret that Barcelona are looking to strengthen their defence in the January transfer window, particularly at centre-back, which has been made a priority by the Catalan decision-makers and Hansi Flick.

Despite a budget that remains tight, the Catalan hierarchy should nevertheless be active in January and three targets appear to stand out, Mundo Deportivo explained midweek.

Alongside Nico Schlotterbeck and Lisandro Martinez, one of them leads to Alessandro Bastoni, whom Flick had nevertheless 'rejected' a few months ago. The reason: the Italian reportedly lacks pace for the Barcelona boss, who even preferred Gerard Martin, reveals Mundo Deportivo journalist Fernando Polo.

Whether he has changed his mind to the point of agreeing to the signing of the Inter player is far from certain.

According to the same source, the 61-year-old manager also reportedly vetoed the arrival of two other players: Aymeric Laporte and Cristian Romero.

The name of the France-born Spain international was reportedly set aside because the club did not want to base a decision solely on his level during the World Cup and apparently had doubts about his ability to maintain that form over the long term. The Argentine, for his part, did not win Flick's favour because he is not left-footed.

The journalist adds that the German's ideal profile is Josko Gvardiol, but a deal for him was too difficult to complete. The problem will probably be the same in January with the Croatia international.

One thing is certain given Mundo Deportivo's revelations: Hansi Flick apparently has the final say on a large share of potential signings.

#1949. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

The first half in north London is brought to an end and Tottenham take a 2-0 lead into the break thanks to goals from Moore and Solanke. Tottenham looked rather lethargic for a lot of that first half but two goals in quick succession has Roberto De Zerbi’s side in control. As the players head off, the DJ pays homage to the late Dolly Parton by blasting out Nine to Five.

Whilst they are still in added time in north London, it is half-time at St James’ Park and Newcastle are level 1-1 with West Brom.

Apter is booked for cynically tripping up Udogie.

Due to a few Charlton injuries, there will be six added minutes.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Tottenham have their second just before the break. Charlton fail to clear their lines inside their own box before Solanke volleys in on the swivel from the penalty spot. Charlton will feel that was definitely an avoidable goal.

Tottenham had looked rather lethargic but they take the lead in emphatic style. The 19-year-old cuts inside from the right and comes across the face of the Charlton penalty area. Moore then strikes it powerfully with his left foot and the ball flies into the roof of the net. Could Brooks have done better in the Charlton goal? Moore will not care.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

Tottenham are currently too slow in possession and are not moving the ball quickly enough, meaning it is easier for Charlton to defend.

West Brom had taken the lead at St James’ Park but Newcastle are back on level terms through summer signing Toure.

A corner from the right ends up coming out to the edge of the box, where Tel takes it first time but his volley goes a long way wide. That moment sums up Tottenham’s evening thus far.

Solanke has a shot from the edge of the box blocked before Gray’s effort with the outside of his right foot is saved well by Brooks down to his left. That looked like it was creeping in so Brooks had to get a hand to that.

Charlton play the corner short and eventually the ball comes in. Asiimwe meets it and has a good chance from eight yards out but his header goes just wide. That was a decent chance for Charlton.

The first booking of the night goes the way of the hosts as Bergvall cynically takes down Apter as the Charlton man drove towards the Tottenham penalty area. You feel like Charlton need to take advantage of opportunities like this if they want to win this tie. The ball is clipped in and it comes off Van Hecke’s head for a corner. Tottenham clear their lines initially but Charlton keep it alive. Docherty strikes it first time from the edge of the Tottenham box and forces Kinsky into a good save diving to his left.

That probably sums up Tottenham’s night thus far. Davies pings a lovely diagonal ball out to Moore in space down Tottenham’s right. Moore waits for the overlapping run of Gray before playing the pass but Gray’s attempted cross from the right side of the box is terrible and goes behind for a goal kick. Roberto De Zerbi is quickly out of his seat!

Roberto De Zerbi was keen to see his side show a reaction to their defeat at Brentford on Saturday. Unsurprisingly, they are dominating possession but have not posed much of a threat going forward.

There has been a goal at St James’ Park and it is the visitors West Brom who have taken the lead over Newcastle. Price has scored directly from a free-kick and the Championship side lead.

A sensational free-kick from Isaac Price to give West Brom the lead at St. James' Park! 🤯Watch the Carabao Cup here! - https://t.co/4BMyhp9stB pic.twitter.com/Pnt78LWFN6

Things have just gone from bad to worse for Charlton. Whilst one of their centre-backs is being stretchered off in Sichenje, their other centre-half Koumetio, who used to be on the books at Liverpool, is also down. Koumetio, like Sichenje, is going to come off. McNamara and Jones, who like Koumetio used to be at Liverpool, are coming on. Charlton have had to change both centre-backs inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Sichenje did try to continue but he has gone back down again and his night appears to be over. The question will be has he done more damage to his knee trying to play on? The stretcher is being brought on and it will be a sorry end to his night.

Moore wins Tottenham a corner out on the right, which summer signing Fernandes will take. His delivery is headed away and the danger is gone.

Sichenje has now got back to his feet so he may have avoided a serious injury but we will see if he can continue. It looks like he will try to continue at least.

Play is halted as Charlton defender Sichenje looks to be in a lot of pain as he bangs the ground in frustration. It appears to be his left knee and the visitors may be forced into an early change.

Inside the opening minute, Solanke thinks he will have a chance on goal as the ball is played in behind but there is too much on it and the ball goes through to Brooks in the Charlton goal.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and we are just moments away from kick-off north London. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Davies, Udogie; Fernandes, Bentancur, Bergvall; Moore, Solanke, Tel. Substitutes: Dubravka, Robertson, Danso, Gallagher, Richarlison, Savio, Porro, Van de Ven, Williams-Barnett.

Charlton: Brooks, Shichenje, Koumetio, Mesik, Asilmwe, Knibbs, Ouma, Apter, Docherty, Alli, Mbick.Substitutes: Okonkwo, Jones, Coventry, Leaburn, Carey, McNamara, Rankin-Costello, Nwamba, Tagoe.

“Tottenham are a top club. Top manager and players so it is a wonderful opportunity to test ourselves. We need to be organised and in the moments we have we want to use our structure to carry a threat. We want to see our structure coming through because we want to evolve. We are a way off these yet, but that is eventually the goal.”

"They got what they deserved"Jamie Redknapp on Spurs' opening day loss against Brentford 😤 pic.twitter.com/mLEb1cCF1x

"I would like to see a reaction"Roberto De Zerbi speaks ahead of Spurs vs Charlton 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/dVIqQBG3wV

After nine years at Anfield, Andy Robertson has swapped Liverpool for Tottenham this summer. He started for Tottenham against Brentford and is on the bench tonight ahead of what could be his first home game for the club.

Omar Marmoush will undergo a medical at Tottenham Hotspur on Wednesday on loan with an obligation to pay Manchester City £60m for the Egypt forward next summer.

Marmoush will become the second signing from City this week after Savinho – who has asked to be referred to as Sávio – completed his move.

City signed Marmoush two seasons ago from Eintracht Frankfurt for £59m and the German club do not have a sell-on clause, meaning they will not receive a fee from the deal.

We will also provide updates from Newcastle’s game against West Brom. The draw for League Cup third round will take place after all the games have been completed tonight.

Our Spurs side to face Charlton! 📋🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/yQuEVgkHbm

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1947. When Football Felt Like Football: A Trip Back to Portsmouth v West Ham, 1992

Tonight’s mid table clash, yep, 10th play 12th, brought back memories of a West Ham United game in Division 1 back in 1992/1993. Without wanting to sound like Paul Whitehouse’s legendary Fast Show character, Ron Manager, and his famous cry of “jumpers for goalposts”, my mind drifted back to the footballing world of the 1990s this morning.

I recall watching the game on ITV, on a programme called the London Match, hosted by Ian St John, and a quick search on YouTube found some footage, with Greavsies side kick being  joined by Glenn Hoddle. Jim Rosenthal was at Fratton Park as part of the commentary team.

Portsmouth featured in the FA Cup semi finals the previous season. West Ham drew 1-1 with Derby County the week before the game, Trevor Morley cancelling out a clearance by Mitchell Thomas which had cannoned off Ludo for an own goal earlier in the game, which kept the Hammers in the top six.

With Billy Bonds at the helm, West Ham were unbeaten in six games, yet faced a Pompey team that had only played twice at home, won both and not conceded. They boasted the prolific striker Guy Whittingham up front, and with Jim Smith in the manager’s seat, were stiff opposition for us. Yet as he said in the warm up the Hammers were one of the favourites to go up.

Pre game the big news was welcoming back Julian Dicks our skipper who came off a three match ban.

The Hammers took the lead just before half time with Clive Allen (main  pic) scoring, yet despite an onslaught of the Pompey goal in the second half they couldn’t add to their tally.

Trevor Morley was denied by the woodwork, while Martin Allen (who was never afraid to shoot from distance) also had a long effort saved.

Happy memories, as it was a time when the club had a greater connection to us, the fans.

I’d settle for a clean sheet and a win tonight, how football has changed or as Ron said “Isn’t it, wasn’t it, marvellous”.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

Great days indeed. The London match was the hangover from ITV losing tv rights to Sky. It was pretty good and we seemed to feature quite allot as Itv regionalised live matches. The production was always good as it was made by the same people that had presented the match for first division football for many years. That also turned out in true hammers fashion to be a topsy turned season for us as we got it over the line on the very last match v Cambridge.

That was a season of heartache for Pompey. Missed out to the Hammers on goal difference for promotion and then to Liverpool in the FA Cup semis for a first Cup Final since 1939. That was a great, entertaining team put together by the Bald Eagle.

Pompey fan – I was at that game. Hope you hammers enjoy the old fashioned nature of Fratton Park tonight…but not too much eh?

#1946. Arsenal injury news: Raya blow leaves Arteta facing a season-defining dilemma

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:35

Mikel Arteta's concern over David Raya has grown beyond the result of the 2-2 draw with Newcastle on Saturday. The Spanish goalkeeper had to leave the pitch in the second half following a collision with William Osula, and has become a source of apprehension at Arsenal.

Still without a definitive diagnosis, the player is due to undergo tests to determine the severity of the problem, but the possibility of missing a few weeks represents a significant setback for Arsenal's plans.

Raya received treatment on the pitch, but continued to show discomfort and was unable to remain in the match. Kepa Arrizabalaga came on in his place, 25 minutes into the second half. In his post-match interview, Arteta did not hide his concern over the situation of his first-choice goalkeeper.

'Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news. Tomorrow, he will have an MRI scan, but at the moment I do not know' - the manager said.

The apprehension is understandable. Raya is not just Arsenal's first-choice goalkeeper: he has become a central piece in the way the team organise themselves defensively and start their moves. His security when coming off his line, ability to play with his feet and involvement in build-up from the back make him a reference point within Arteta's model. Finding a replacement capable of reproducing all of these characteristics is no simple task.

Arteta's first alternative is set. Signed to join the squad and provide depth in the position, Kepa is Raya's immediate understudy and took over as soon as the Spaniard had to leave the pitch against Newcastle.

Should the injury rule the first-choice goalkeeper out for a few weeks, the former Real Madrid man will have the opportunity to show that he can sustain the team's competitive level at an important point in the season.

The question, however, involves more than simply filling the spot. Kepa has experience at big clubs and knows the demands of playing decisive matches, but his record also includes episodes that fuel doubts about his consistency. His performance against Newcastle, for example, was not enough to remove the question marks over his ability to take over as first choice without Arsenal suffering a drop in performance.

The most uncomfortable memory for supporters is the League Cup final last season against Manchester City. On that occasion, a mistake by Kepa carried weight in the result and reinforced the criticism of the goalkeeper.

While an isolated episode does not determine a player's ability, the current situation demands that he offer answers on the pitch, especially if he has to take over the position for a longer period.

The challenge also lies in the differences between the styles of the two Spaniards. Raya offers a combination of reflexes, positioning and quality in distribution that allows Arsenal to maintain their approach even when under opposition pressure. Kepa will need to show security both in his interventions and in his decisions with the ball, preventing the change in goal from causing significant alterations to the defensive functioning.

In addition to Kepa, Arsenal have Illan Meslier in the squad. The Frenchman appears as another possibility for Arteta, although he is behind the Spaniard in the goalkeeping hierarchy.

His presence widens the options available, but does not necessarily mean the manager is willing to promote an immediate change in the order of preference.

Giving Meslier an opportunity would be a decision involving risks and benefits. On the one hand, it would allow Arsenal to assess an alternative in a position that may require more than one player over the course of the season.

On the other, backing a goalkeeper who does not currently occupy the first position in the contest could represent an even bigger change in a system that would already need to adapt to Raya's absence.

The possibility of looking for a reinforcement in the January transfer window may also enter the debate, particularly if the tests confirm a more serious injury and a lengthy recovery period. Even so, signing another goalkeeper would not be an automatic solution. Besides market availability, Arsenal would need to find a player who offered the conditions to take over as first choice and adapt quickly to Arteta's demands.

The timing of the season makes the situation even more delicate. Arsenal lead the Premier League and also have important commitments in the Champions League. In the coming weeks, the team will face opponents such as Borussia Dortmund, Manchester City, Brentford, Tottenham and Real Madrid, a sequence that will demand concentration and consistency in every area.

#1945. Opposition insight for Milan-Frosinone: Form, injuries, predicted XI and more

AC Milan are looking to make it three consecutive wins tomorrow, but a high-flying newcomer in Frosinone could make that difficult.

Ruben Amorim and his men have an opportunity to really establish some momentum tomorrow evening, picking up where they left off before the break. However, it won’t be an easy game against Massimiliano Alvani’s Frosinone, who have impressed everyone so far.

Amorim even warned in his press conference that it will be a difficult one, especially since the Canarini have such a direct style.

➤ Manager: Massimiliano Alvini ➤ Form (all comps): W-D-W-W-L (most recent) ➤ Top scorer (Serie A): Raimondo – 8 ➤ Most assists (Serie A): Kvernadze, Schmid and Ghedjemis – 4 ➤ Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

#1944. Hammers favourite reveals Nuno’s part in his decision to quit West Ham

One of the major disappointments from this summer of change was seeing Hammers’ academy graduate Freddie Potts leave the club where he’d been since he was a seven year old. A ten million transfer fee justified the move in most fans’ minds, but there was still a sense of unfulfilled promise, despite Potts’ finally achieving his dream of a Premier League debut for the team he loved and had supported as a child.

In a candid interview today with BBC.co.uk, Potts reveals why he chose to quit West Ham United.

Without putting too fine a point on it, the whole move to Belgian Champions FC Brugge came about through manager Nuno Espirito Santo’s selection choices and Potts being sidelined, as he explained:

“In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren’t as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and said ‘let’s explore options because this season I’m 22, turning 23’,” Potts said.

“It’s a massive part of my career and I wanted to play.”

Nuno’s decision to limit Potts’ game time led to his decision to quit the club

Subsequently the interest from Brugge- now competing in the Champions League against the likes of Liverpool this very week – arose and Potts grabbed at the chance:

“The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn’t really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.

“I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career.”

And who can blame him: Freddie lines up against Liverpool this week in the Champions League – the same week in which his old club head for a second division mid table scrap with Portsmouth. Good decision young man. Go and win it.

He was very good for most of the season but maybe understandably his form tailed off a little bit late on, with the team struggling.

Recent months have been chaotic at St James’ Park to say the least but with injuries beginning to clear, the returning Dan Burn playing alongside Malick Thiaw against Fulham and Arsenal, they look like a partnership that can do well for United this season. Also, Jurgen Klopp has started Malick Thiaw in three of his last four team selections with Germany and the United defender has played well.

#1939. West Ham will get back on track if they follow competitor example – report

The difference between success and failure in this division is measured in hundreds of millions of pounds. To the three promoted sides comes the financial mushroom cloud of Premier League cash – a veritable explosion to enable survival in the top tier – but to those who fail to climb out of the Championship – especially those with big budgets – comes financial obscurity and the very real risk of further budget slashing just to stay afloat.

Last season, Championship teams between them lost a worrying £300 million plus: An unsustainable model for football club survival and West Ham, with hugely diminished parachute payments, would face further swinging cuts to stay solvent. So promotion at the first attempt is crucial.

The Hammers would do well to take a leaf out of competitor Wolverhampton Wanderers’ books. Like West Ham, Wolves have stuttered without hitting top form and yet there they sit, third in the Championship. As footballleagueworld.co.uk report, they’ve ground out an impressive sequence of results:

“if Wolves haven’t always impressed with their performances, they have found a way of getting results, and they head into the Derby game unbeaten in seven, picking up 17 points in that period.”

“Wolves are just getting it done. Even when they haven’t been turning up (performances), they’ve been doing enough. So, it worries me that if they turn it on, and click into gear, and reach another level, they could be the ones.”

Winning ugly, they used to call it. And West Ham need to learn the lesson from their Black Country opponents and start grinding out results even if they are not playing fluid, attractive football.

Because it’s all about the points. And what do points make?

#1938. PSG: Why Doue's serious injury could derail Luis Enrique's season

By Axel Clody | 23 Nov 2026 07:48

PSG's 3-2 win over Nice on Saturday at the Allianz Riviera, in round 11 of Ligue 1, brought terrible news for Luis Enrique.

Shortly before half-time, Desire Doue, who had scored a goal minutes earlier, collapsed to the ground after twisting his right knee while attempting a dribble. Amid cries of pain, the winger had to leave the pitch on a stretcher when substituted.

Speaking to Ligue 1+, the Spanish manager said in advance that Doue's injury 'was serious', a fear confirmed on Sunday. Imaging results found that the PSG number 14 has suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament and will have to undergo surgery in the coming days.

PSG have not disclosed a recovery timeline, but cases similar to Desire Doue's that require surgical intervention show that players usually spend at least six months in the medical department. The 21-year-old Frenchman should therefore only return to action at the end of May.

In the most optimistic scenario, Doue would be fit in time for a possible Champions League final, to be played on 5 June at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, Spain. However, depending on the strategy PSG adopt to cover for the young winger's absence, the success of this season is at risk.

Signed in August 2024 from Rennes for £42.5m (€50m), Desire Doue became one of Luis Enrique's trusted men, so much so that he was an important part of the rotation in his debut season (16 goals and 14 assists in 61 matches) and was named man of the match in the European final against Inter Milan, when he scored twice.

In 2025-26, the French attacking midfielder had his run at PSG interrupted by two muscle injuries, but still managed 13 goals and eight assists in 40 matches, as well as scoring his penalty as PSG won back-to-back Champions League titles against Arsenal. And after representing his country at the World Cup, Doue was enjoying an overwhelming start to the season.

As a reward for his good form at PSG, Doue began to gain more space in the France team under Zinedine Zidane, who even said that he reminded him of himself when he played as a midfielder, because of his personality of always wanting to improve by listening to older players.

More than the impact in the final third, Doue is also a joker for the PSG manager because of his two-footedness, able to play on either wing.

The Frenchman had been playing on the left in recent weeks as a replacement for Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, who also suffered an anterior cruciate ligament rupture in his right knee during the win over Barcelona on 20 October, in the Champions League.

The Georgian underwent surgery and should only be available to the Spanish manager in mid-April. With two heavyweight absences in the attacking system, PSG must ask themselves whether it is necessary to reinforce the area when the transfer window reopens, or whether the current squad will be enough to remain competitive on all fronts.

If PSG conclude that the solution lies in the market, they will have to do very meticulous work to find someone who fits Luis Enrique's playing philosophy, based on high intensity and constant movement, and who is available to leave in January. It is true that there is no shortage of talents around the world who fit those requirements, but the certainty is that no signing would be cheap, nor a guarantee of immediate success.

On the other hand, if PSG give a vote of confidence to the current players, which at the moment is the public discourse, they will have to get more out of their players. 2025 Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembele has suffered from different physical problems in 2026-27, so much so that he has constantly been placed on a load management regime.

Ferran Torres, signed from Barcelona for £42.5m (€50m), had an exciting start at PSG, with seven goals in the first six matches. However, as in his Camp Nou days, the Spanish forward began to fluctuate and went eight games without scoring, ending the drought against Nice.

Maghnes Akliouche, bought from Monaco for £42.5m (€50m), has not yet reached his full potential (two goals and three assists in 16 matches), which is normal for a newcomer. But the lack of prior experience as a protagonist in the Champions League raises doubts over whether the 24-year-old Frenchman is able to make a difference for PSG.

It is a similar case to Mika Godts, acquired from Ajax for £46.8m (€55m), but with the aggravating factor that he is still going through the process of adapting to French football. As he is still 21, the Belgian winger has been inconsistent at PSG, with two goals and two assists in 12 matches.

Finally, Senny Mayulu (20) and Quentin Ndjantou (19) are academy gems still looking to establish themselves among the professionals. The Spanish manager does have the possibility of pushing Nuno Mendes and/or Achraf Hakimi forward, but that would create a problem at full-back.

PSG have seven more games until the winter break, but with Ligue 1, the Coupe de France and the Intercontinental Cup, it is undeniable that the mission of chasing a third successive Champions League title has become much harder without Doue.
